findings.title: Semgrep app token committed in tracked example file
findings.description: SEMGREP_APP_TOKEN is a 64-character hexadecimal value in a file that .gitignore explicitly re-includes (!.env.mcp.example). The GitHub repository is public. This is not a placeholder. .env.example uses a real placeholder for the same variable.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1) Clone https://github.com/aaron-howard/service-certify. 2) Read .env.mcp.example line 15. 3) Call Semgrep App API with that token (findings, scans, org metadata depending on token scope). Do not replay the token in this report.
findings.impact: Unauthorized use of the Semgrep org token: read findings, trigger scans, or otherwise act as the token owner until revoked.
findings.recommendation: Revoke the token in Semgrep immediately. Replace the tracked value with a placeholder (your_semgrep_app_token). Keep real tokens only in .env.mcp.local (gitignored). If this repo was ever public or forked, treat history as exposed; rotate and review Semgrep audit logs.
findings.playbook: 1. Revoke the credential in Semgrep org settings. 2. Rotate: create a new token, store only in gitignored local env. 3. Scrub: replace the committed value with a placeholder; consider git filter-repo if the token must leave history. 4. Force-push only if you accept history rewrite cost for a public repo. 5. Audit exposure window from commit 137c49a to revoke time. 6. Check Semgrep audit logs for unexpected API use.

findings.title: Admin role is sticky and never demoted on profile sync
findings.description: createOrUpdateUser promotes allowlisted emails to admin but never clears role when the email leaves ADMIN_EMAILS. Comment states never downgrade admins on profile sync. requireAdmin trusts users.role.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1) User email is on ADMIN_EMAILS; they log in and get role admin. 2) Operator removes them from ADMIN_EMAILS. 3) They sign in again; createOrUpdateUser skips the role patch. 4) They call practiceQuestions.listByTrackCode / gradeAnswers with mode full, and admin/exportQuestions.exportAllQuestions, and receive the full bank.
findings.impact: Former admins keep full-mock and export access indefinitely. Crown-jewel question bank plus answers and explanations.
findings.recommendation: On every sync, set role from the current allowlist (admin if isAdminEmail(email) else user), or add an explicit revoke mutation and run it when the allowlist changes. Do not treat admin as a one-way latch.

findings.title: Auth binds to any user sharing JWT email when workosId misses
findings.description: getAuthenticatedUser looks up by workosId, then falls back to by_email.unique() on identity.email. requireAdmin uses this helper. createOrUpdateUser does not use the fallback (workosId only). by_email is not a unique constraint. Convex functions are callable with a WorkOS JWT without going through SvelteKit.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1) Admin Convex row still has email E, but workosId no longer matches a new identity that presents email E (email change leftover, IdP reuse, or stale email field). 2) Attacker authenticates to WorkOS so the JWT email is E. 3) Attacker calls Convex directly with that JWT and never calls createOrUpdateUser. 4) getAuthenticatedUser misses workosId, binds to the existing row, and requireAdmin succeeds. 5) Attacker lists/grades full mode and exports the bank.
findings.impact: Account bind / admin impersonation without matching WorkOS subject. Full question bank if the matched row is admin.
findings.recommendation: Authorize only by workosId. Remove the email fallback. Optionally patch workosId on a verified email-change flow. Add a unique constraint or application-level uniqueness on email.

findings.title: Full practice answer key committed in public git
findings.description: The public repository contains the practice bank with correctIndex, explanations, and sourceUrls (2072 correctIndex entries). Convex listByTrackCode strips answers for clients and requireAdmin gates full mode, so the running API treats answers as sensitive while git publishes them.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1) Clone the public repo. 2) Parse src/convex/seed/devQuestionBank.ts. 3) Read every prompt, correctIndex, and explanation. No account or admin role required.
findings.impact: The product crown jewel (full answer key) is public. Admin-only full mock on the API does not protect the key.
findings.recommendation: If the bank is meant to stay private: move seed data out of git, load from a private store or Convex-only seed, and purge history. If open content is intended: drop the admin secrecy model and document that answers are public.

findings.title: OAuth login authorization URL omits CSRF state
findings.description: getOAuthAuthorizationUrl passes clientId, provider, and redirectUri only. Login sets provider and post-auth redirect cookies but no nonce. Callback authenticateWithCode uses code and clientId only. Step-up helper already supports state.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1) Attacker starts OAuth and obtains a WorkOS authorization URL (or a code bound to the attacker). 2) Victim is induced to hit /auth/callback?code=... in their browser (login CSRF). 3) Callback sets httpOnly cookies for the attacker identity. 4) Victim's later practice progress writes to the attacker account.
findings.impact: Session fixation onto the attacker account. No payments in this app; still account confusion and progress theft/pollution.
findings.recommendation: Generate a csrf state, store it httpOnly, pass it to getAuthorizationUrl, and verify it in the callback before authenticateWithCode. Use PKCE if WorkOS supports it for this flow. Mirror the existing step-up state option.

findings.title: deleteAccount skips step-up auth_time check
findings.description: SvelteKit POST /api/account/delete requires isRecentAuthentication on the WorkOS JWT. Convex mutation deleteAccount only calls getAuthenticatedUser. Convex is reachable with a bearer JWT.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1) Attacker steals a still-valid WorkOS access token (XSS on a subdomain, malware, leaked HAR). 2) Token auth_time is older than the 5-minute step-up window, so the website delete route returns 403. 3) Attacker ConvexHttpClient.setAuth(token) then api.auth.deleteAccount. 4) User row and progress are deleted.
findings.impact: Destructive account wipe without recent re-auth. Needs a stolen access token; bypasses the only step-up control.
findings.recommendation: Enforce recent auth_time (or a server-side step-up flag) inside the Convex mutation. Treat the HTTP route as UX, not the security boundary.

findings.title: MCP servers pin npx packages at @latest
findings.description: Committed Cursor MCP config runs npx -y convex@latest and npx -y @upstash/mcp-server@latest. Those resolve at agent start, not at lockfile install.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1) A malicious or compromised latest of convex or @upstash/mcp-server is published. 2) A developer opens the repo in Cursor; MCP auto-starts npx. 3) The package runs with CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY / Upstash credentials from env. 4) Attacker gets deploy-key or Redis credential scope for that workstation.
findings.impact: Developer-workstation supply chain. Not a production HTTP path. Credentials in MCP env are the blast radius.
findings.recommendation: Pin exact versions (convex@1.x.y, @upstash/mcp-server@x.y.z). Prefer npm-installed binaries over npx @latest. Integrity pinning where the client supports it.

findings.title: No CODEOWNERS on GitHub workflow paths
findings.description: Four workflows exist. Actions are SHA-pinned and contents: read is set. There is no CODEOWNERS file, so workflow edits do not require a designated reviewer.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1) Attacker lands a PR that edits .github/workflows (poisoned pipeline). 2) A maintainer who is not a CI owner approves a drive-by change. 3) Later workflow run executes attacker-controlled steps if permissions expand or secrets are added.
findings.impact: Lower bar to persist CI persistence. Current jobs are relatively locked down (SHA pins, contents: read); this is a process control gap on workflow files.
findings.recommendation: Add CODEOWNERS requiring review on .github/workflows/** (and optionally .github/dependabot.yml). Keep action SHA pins.
